questions.stem: A 25-year-old patient presents with a genetic anomaly affecting the activity of disaccharidases produced by the intestinal epithelial cells. These enzymes are responsible for the digestion of various disaccharides into monosaccharides, which can then be absorbed into the bloodstream. After consuming a meal consisting of milk and oatmeal, both of which contain disaccharides, which of the following would you expect to find in higher levels in this patient compared to a healthy individual?

options.label: A
options.text: Galactose and fructose in the blood.

options.label: C
options.text: Maltose, sucrose, and lactose in the stool

questions.answerText: Maltose, sucrose, and lactose in the stool
questions.solutionHtml:
an>

 

Option A: Galactose and fructose in the blood would be lower, not higher, because these monosaccharides result from the digestion of lactose and sucrose, respectively, which is impaired in this patient.

 

Option B: Starch in the stool would not necessarily be higher because starch digestion begins with salivary and pancreatic amylase, not disaccharidases.

 

Option D: Glycogen in the muscles would be unaffected directly by disaccharidase activity as it is dependent on the uptake of glucose from the blood, which would be reduced due to the malabsorption of its precursor disaccharides.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

Starch: digested to small oligosaccharides and maltose but produce lower quantity of glucose due to deficiency of the brush border disaccharidases, which include sucrase and lactase. So, Sucrose and lactose will not be cleaved and will accumulate.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e:  p 538, 599



Harper 30/e: p 538, 599

questions.stem: A patient with a long-standing history of type I diabetes mellitus has been diligently adhering to insulin therapy, yet consistently records fasting and postprandial blood glucose levels that exceed the normal range. To assist in better glucose regulation, a dietician suggests an increased intake of dietary fiber. Among the Option listed below, which type of dietary fiber is most beneficial for managing blood glucose levels in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
ke pectin particularly valuable for patients with diabetes who need to manage blood glucose levels.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A: Cellulose: These are polymers of glucose. It retains water in feces; promotes peristalsis and increases bowel action. It is the starting material for production of fibres, celluloids, nitrocellulose, and plastics.

 

Option B: Hemicellulose: These include pentoses, hexoses and uronic acid, which retains water in feces and increases bile acid excretion.

 

Option C: Lignin: They are aromatic alcohols with hypocholesterolemic, antioxidant action and also increases bile acid excretion.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Dietary fibers are classified as soluble (pectin, gums, mucilages) or insoluble (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin). Soluble fibers like pectin form viscous gels that slow digestion and absorption of carbohydrates, making them particularly beneficial for blood glucose management in diabetes. Pectin is found in fruits (especially apples, citrus fruits), berries, and some vegetables. Insoluble fibers primarily improve bowel health and regularity without significantly affecting blood glucose levels directly.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e: P 156-158.



Harper 30/e: P 156-158.

altosazone: Maltosazone crystals tend to have a "pom-pom" or "sunflower" shape with radial striations, which does not match the crystals in the image.

The osazone test is to distinguish between different reducing sugars based on the characteristic crystalline structures they form when reacted with phenylhydrazine.

questions.stem: A middle-aged woman who has recently experienced several episodes of diarrhea was advised by her general practitioner to consume fructans like inulin, which serve as prebiotics due to their non-digestibility. What is the primary reason for the resistance of such carbohydrates to digestion in the upper gastrointestinal tract?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Beta configuration of anomeric C2

 

This is the primary reason fructans like inulin resist digestion in the upper GI tract:

Fructans consist of fructose molecules linked together, and in fructose (unlike glucose), the anomeric carbon is C2 rather than C1. The beta configuration at this anomeric C2 carbon creates β glycosidic linkages between fructose units in inulin. Human digestive enzymes in the intestine (like amylase, maltase, sucrase, etc.) are specific for hydrolyzing α-glycosidic bonds, particularly those found in starches and common disaccharides. These enzymes cannot break the β-glycosidic linkages at the anomeric C2 carbon in fructans, making these carbohydrates non-digestible in the upper GI tract.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Beta configuration of anomeric C1 - This is incorrect because in fructose molecules, C1 is not the anomeric carbon. In fructose, the anomeric carbon is C2, which makes this answer choice fundamentally incorrect for describing fructans.

 

Option B. Low pH of the stomach - While the acidic environment of the stomach can affect some carbohydrates, this is not the primary reason for fructans' resistance to digestion. Many digestible carbohydrates also pass through the same acidic environment without becoming resistant to digestion. The specific glycosidic linkages, not stomach acidity, determine digestibility.

 

Option D. Presence of α-Glycosidic linkage - This is incorrect because Inulin contain β-glycosidic linkages, not α-glycosidic linkages. α-Glycosidic linkages are actually digestible by human enzymes (like amylase, maltase), so their presence would make a carbohydrate more digestible, not less.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The key mechanism that makes fructans like inulin function as effective prebiotics is their resistance to digestion in the upper GI tract due to the beta configuration at the anomeric C2 carbon. This structural feature creates β-glycosidic linkages between fructose units that human digestive enzymes cannot break down. As a result, these carbohydrates pass intact to the lower intestine where they selectively stimulate the growth of beneficial bacteria, particularly Bifidobacteria and Lactobacilli.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with chronic congestive heart failure (CCF) has been prescribed digoxin, which enhances cardiac contractility and rhythm. Digoxin comprises a sugar moiety and a non-sugar (aglycone) component linked via an oxygen atom. What is the chemical classification of digoxin based on this structure?
questions.solutionHtml:
"Calibri",sans-serif">Glycosides contain a sugar and a non-sugar component (aglycone) linked together by O-Glycosidic linkage.

 

 

Explanation:

 

Option B: Glycoprotein: When the carbohydrate chains are attached to a polypeptide chain it is called a proteoglycan and if the carbohydrate content is less than 10%, it is generally named as a glycoprotein.

 

Option C: Oligosaccharide: Further addition of sugar groups to a Trisaccharide produces tetrasaccharides, pentasaccharides and so on, known as oligosaccharides.

 

Option D: Polysaccharide: Polymerized products of many monosaccharide units.

 

They may be:

 

  1. Homoglycans (single kind of monosaccharides, e.g. starch, glycogen and cellulose)
  2. Heteroglycans (two or more different monosaccharides, e.g. hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulphate).

 

Educational Objective:

 

The chemical structure of digoxin is a cardiac glycoside, which has therapeutic effects in heart failure by increasing the force of cardiac muscle contraction.

questions.stem: A clinician evaluates a patient with decreased visual acuity and diagnoses cataracts, a condition characterized by clouding of the lens. The development of cataracts can be influenced by various metabolic factors, including the accumulation of certain substances within the lens. Among the following, which substance's accumulation is most commonly associated with the formation of cataracts?
questions.solutionHtml:
e="text-align:justify">Explanation:

 

Option A: While high blood glucose levels are a risk factor for cataract development, glucose itself does not accumulate in the lens to the extent that it directly causes cataracts. Instead, its conversion to sorbitol is the main issue.

 

Option B: Galactose can lead to cataracts, primarily in conditions like galactosemia, where there's an inability to metabolize galactose properly, leading to its accumulation in various tissues, including the lens. This option is also plausible but less common than the accumulation of sorbitol.

 

Option C: Sugar amines are not directly associated with cataract formation. While glycation of lens proteins by sugars can contribute to cataractogenesis, the accumulation of specific sugar amines is not a well-recognized cause.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • In Diabetes mellitus, in the lens by polyol pathway, glucose converted to sorbitol by the enzyme Aldose reductase
  • In galactosemia, Dulcitol or Galactitol is responsible for cataract
  • Sorbitol, Dulcitol are sugar alcohols.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e p205.



Harper 30/e p205.

questions.stem: Cellulose, a major component of plant cell walls, plays a critical role in providing structural support. Given its biological significance and chemical composition, how is cellulose best categorized?
questions.solutionHtml:
p>

Option A: Cellulose is not a lipoprotein; it does not contain lipid or protein components.

 

Option B: It is not a starch polysaccharide. Starch, another plant polysaccharide, is composed of α-glucose units and serves as an energy storage molecule, whereas cellulose serves a structural role.

 

Option D: Cellulose is not a glycoprotein; it does not contain any protein or covalently bound oligosaccharide chains.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Foods contain a variety of other polysaccharides known as nonstarch polysaccharides.
  • They are not digested by human enzymes and form the major components of dietary fibre.
  • E.g.: cellulose from plant cell walls (a glucose polymer) and Inulin, the storage carbohydrate in some plants (a fructose polymer).

 

Ref: Harper 30/e p153.



Harper 30/e p153.

questions.stem: Dextran, a complex branched polysaccharide, has been utilized in various medical applications. One specific use of dextran is in the management of hypovolemia. Based on this application, is it accurate to consider dextran as a plasma volume expander?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) True.

 

Option A:

 

Dextran consists of glucose monomers joined in different Linkages (α 1, 6 and α 1, 4 and α 1, 3). It can be used as Plasma Volume Expander, which are high mol wt. substances that exert colloid osmotic pressure and retain fluid in the vascular component.

 

Substances used are:

 

  • Human albumin
  • Dextran
  • Hydroxyethyl starch (Hetastarch)
  • Degraded gelatine polymer.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Dextran is indeed used as a plasma volume expander in clinical settings. By increasing the osmotic pressure in the blood vessels, it helps to retain fluid within the circulatory system, thereby expanding plasma volume. This is particularly useful in treating hypovolemia or shock.

 

Ref: Vasudevan 9/e p 79.



Vasudevan 9/e p 79.

quot;,sans-serif">Explanation:

Option B: 3rd Epimer of Glucose – Allose

To correctly identify epimeric carbon atoms in carbohydrate chemistry, noting that epimers are sugars that differ only in the configuration around one specific carbon atom.

questions.stem: Among the statements provided below, each delves into different aspects of stereochemistry and carbohydrate chemistry. Identify the statement that is accurately described.

options.label: A
options.text: Equimolar mixture of optical isomers are called as Racemic Mixture

options.label: C
options.text: Mutarotation is a property of C2 atom

options.label: D
options.text: The penultimate carbon atom in Glucose is C-2

questions.answerText: Equimolar mixture of optical isomers are called as Racemic Mixture
questions.solutionHtml:
wo isomers.

 

Explanation:

 

Option B: Fructose is part of what is termed "invert sugar" when combined with glucose, especially after the hydrolysis of sucrose. The statement is misleading as it implies fructose alone is invert sugar, which is not accurate.

 

Option C: Mutarotation is the change in the optical rotation due to the change in the equilibrium between two anomers, often related to the anomeric carbon, which in glucose and many other sugars is C1, not C2.

 

Option D: The penultimate carbon atom in glucose, a six-carbon sugar (hexose), is C-5, not C-2.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Racemic Mixture: Equimolar mixture of optical isomers which has no net rotation of plane polarized light. Sucrose is Otherwise Called Invert Sugar. Sucrose is dextrorotatory and on hydrolysis it yields a mixture of dextrorotatory Glucose and levorotatory Fructose.  Because of the strong levorotatory nature of fructose, Sucrose on hydrolysis becomes levorotatory. Hence, Sucrose is called invert sugar.

 

Ref: Vasudevan 9/e p 71.



Vasudevan 9/e p 71.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs represent enantiomers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) D-Mannose and L-Mannose

 

Option C:

 

D-Mannose and L-Mannose are enantiomers of each other, as they are mirror images and cannot be superimposed. The ‘D’ and ‘L’ notation indicates that they are pairs of enantiomers, with each being the mirror image of the other.

 

Educational Objective:

 

D and L Isomerism [Enantiomers]

 

  • Difference in the orientation of the H and OH group around the Penultimate Carbon atom results in two mirror images known as D and L isomers (Enantiomers).
  • The penultimate carbon atom is named as Reference Carbon atom.
  • The penultimate carbon atom in Glucose and Fructose is C-5.
  • Most of the naturally occurring Monosaccharides are D isomers.

 

Examples of Enantiomers

 

  • D-Glucose and L-Glucose
  • D-Fructose and L-Fructose
  • D-Mannose and L-Mannose
  • D-Glyceraldehyde and L-Glyceraldehyde.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e p153.



erence Carbon atom.

questions.stem: A patient with a history of acute glomerulonephritis, who is currently under treatment, attends a routine follow-up appointment. The focus is on the integrity and function of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) in relation to kidney function. Which mucopolysaccharide present in the GBM is primarily responsible for maintaining the charge-based filtration function of the kidney?
questions.solutionHtml:
ont-size:12pt">Explanation:

 

Option B: Chondroitin sulphate: present in the ground substance of connective tissues which is distributed in cartilage, bone, tendons, cornea and skin.

 

Option C: Hyaluronic acid: present in connective tissues, tendons, synovial fluid and vitreous humor and acts as a lubricant and shock absorber in joint cavities.

 

Option D: Keratan sulphate: only GAG, which does not contain uronic acid and found in cornea and tendons, thereby maintaining corneal transparency.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Heparan sulphate is a key component of the glomerular basement membrane and is vital for its normal function. It provides the GBM with a negative charge, which is essential for the selective filtration of molecules based on size and charge, preventing the passage of negatively charged proteins such as albumin into the urine.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e:  p 638, Lippincott 7/e : P 159



Harper 30/e: p 638, Lippincott 7/e : P 159

questions.stem: A middle-aged man presents with a diagnosis of mucopolysaccharidosis, characterized by the accumulation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). One GAG that has accumulated is known to play a critical role in the charge selectiveness of the renal glomerular membrane. Which of the following GAGs is responsible for maintaining the charge selectiveness of the renal glomerular membrane?
questions.solutionHtml:
lanation:

 

Option B: Dermatan sulphate: found in skin, blood vessels and heart valves and determines the elasticity of heart valve and skin.

 

Option C: Hyaluronic acid: present in connective tissues, tendons, synovial fluid and vitreous humor and acts as a lubricant and shock absorber in joint cavities.

 

Option D: Keratan sulphate: only GAG, which does not contain uronic acid and found in cornea and tendons, thereby maintaining corneal transparency.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Heparan sulfate is a key component of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and contributes to its negative charge. This charge barrier is essential for the selective filtration of molecules based on size and charge. 

 

Ref: Harper 30/e: p 638, Lippincott 6/ed: p 159



Harper 30/e: p 638, Lippincott 6/ed: p 159

questions.stem: A clinician is explaining the importance of various glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in the human body to a group of medical students. One topic of discussion is the essential role certain GAGs play in maintaining corneal transparency, a crucial property for proper vision. Which GAG is primarily responsible for this function?
questions.solutionHtml:
e="text-align:justify">In the eye, they lie between collagen fibril and play a critical role in corneal transparency.

 

Explanation:

 

Option B: Chondroitin sulphate: present in the ground substance of connective tissues which is distributed in cartilage, bone, tendons, cornea, and skin.

 

Option C: Dermatan sulphate: Found in skin, blood vessels and heart valves and determines the elasticity of heart valve and skin.

 

Option D: Hyaluronic acid: present in connective tissues, tendons, synovial fluid and vitreous humor and acts as a lubricant and shock absorber in joint cavities.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Keratan sulphate is the GAG that plays a significant role in maintaining corneal transparency. It is highly sulfated, which facilitates the arrangement of collagen fibers in the cornea in a uniformly spaced pattern, essential for the cornea's transparency.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e:  p 638, Lippincott 7/e: P 159

questions.stem: In the structural hierarchy of proteoglycans, which are crucial to the extracellular matrix's organization, one particular component forms the backbone to which the protein-bound glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains are attached. This backbone allows the proteoglycan to maintain its structure and function. Which of the following is the backbone component of proteoglycan molecules?
questions.solutionHtml:
if">Explanation:

 

Option A: Heparan sulphate is a type of glycosaminoglycan that binds to core proteins but is not the backbone itself.

 

Option B: Keratan sulphate is another glycosaminoglycan present on proteoglycans but again does not serve as the backbone.

 

Option D: Dermatan sulphate is a glycosaminoglycan that is typically found linked to a protein as part of a proteoglycan but is not the central backbone molecule.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Hyaluronic acid is the backbone of proteoglycan aggregates in the extracellular matrix. It provides a central core that other proteoglycans attach to non-covalently, forming large, complex structures that contribute to the matrix's function.

 

Ref: Vasudevan 9/e p 80.

questions.stem: During a pediatric rotation, a medical student observes the management of a child presenting with acute gastroenteritis and signs of dehydration. The attending physician prescribes oral rehydration solution (ORS). The student learns that the efficacy of ORS is partly due to its facilitation of glucose absorption, which in turn enhances electrolyte and water uptake in the intestines. Which glucose transporter is primarily responsible for the glucose absorption facilitated by ORS in the intestinal mucosa?
questions.solutionHtml:
p style="text-align:justify"> 

Option B.  SGLT-2: SGLT-2 is defective in congenital renal glycosuria

 

Option C. GLUT 4:  Insulin-mediated glucose uptake. Involved in Type 2 diabetes mellitus

 

Option D.  GLUT 2: Enables the pancreas to monitor the glucose level, thereby adjusts the rate of insulin secretion.

 

Educational Objective:

 

SGLT 1 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 1) is responsible for the absorption of glucose in the small intestine. It cotransports sodium and glucose from the intestinal lumen into enterocytes, thereby facilitating the absorption of water and electrolytes, which is the principle behind the effectiveness of ORS.

questions.stem: Assertion (A): After overnight fasting, levels of glucose transporters are reduced in adipocytes. Reasoning (R): Adipocytes are insulin-sensitive tissues and as an early response to the hormone, the glucose transporters are externalized.

options.label: A
options.text: A as well as R are right, and R is a correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: A is right but R is a wrong statement

options.label: C
options.text: A is wrong but R is a right statement

options.label: D
options.text: A and R both are wrong

questions.answerText: A as well as R are right, and R is a correct explanation of A
questions.solutionHtml:
ect explanation of A

 

Option A:

 

  • GLUT-4 and Insulin: Glucose uptake into muscle and adipose tissue is fully controlled by insulin, which is secreted by the beta cells of pancreas in response to an increased glucose concentration in the blood.
  • In fasting state, the glucose transporter of muscle and adipose tissue (GLUT-4) is in intracellular vesicles. As insulin secretion falls in the fasting state, the receptors are internalized, reducing glucose uptake.
  • In Fed state: An early response to insulin, migration of these vesicles to the cell surface takes place, where they fuse with the plasma membrane, exposing active glucose transporters.
  • These insulin-sensitive tissues only take up glucose from the bloodstream to any significant extent in the presence of the hormone.

 

Educational Objective:

 

After overnight fasting, insulin levels in the body are low. In insulin-sensitive tissues like adipocytes, low insulin levels lead to a decrease in the number of glucose transporters (such as GLUT4) present on the cell membrane because insulin is required to stimulate the translocation of these transporters from the intracellular stores to the cell surface.

 

Ref: Harper 30/e p192.



Harper 30/e p192.

Explanation

 

Options A: Dysfunctional glucagon receptors typically would not result in skin changes like those described. Glucagon is a catabolic hormone that raises blood glucose levels.

 

Options B: Dysfunctional EGF receptors are associated with various cellular dysfunctions and cancer, not typically with the skin changes seen in acanthosis nigricans.

 

Options D: Only inhibition leads to insulin resistance.

 

Educational Objective

 

Acanthosis nigrican’s, is closely related to insulin resistance. The darkened skin patches are due to hyperinsulinemia that occurs secondary to insulin receptor inhibition, leading to increased insulin-like growth factor activity on skin cells.

Explanation:

 

  • GLUT4 is the major glucose transporter seen in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.
  • GLUT4 is under the control of insulin.
  • Insulin promotes the translocation of intracellular GLUT4 molecules to the cell surface and thus increases glucose uptake.
  • In Type 2 diabetes mellitus, membrane GLUT4 is reduced causing insulin resistance in muscle and fat cells.
  • In diabetes, entry of glucose into muscle is only half of normal cells.

questions.stemHtml: A 42-year-old visits a local clinic for a routine check-up. The healthcare provider at the clinic performs an Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) to assess his glucose metabolism. The results are plotted on a graph showing plasma glucose levels over time after a glucose load. Based on the graph shown, what is your interpretation of the patient’s OGTT results?

options.label: A
options.text: Symptoms of Diabetes mellitus with inconclusive blood glucose values

options.label: D
options.text: Follow-up of a case of Diabetes mellitus

questions.solutionHtml:
>

 

Explanation:

 

Based on the graph provided, which shows plasma glucose levels after a glucose load:

  • The normal curve rises to about 140 mg/dL and then returns to baseline (~90 mg/dL) within 2 hours.
  • The diabetic curve spikes up to ~300 mg/dL at 1 hour and remains significantly elevated (well above 200 mg/dL) even at 2 hours.
  • the Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) is interpreted as follows:
  • Normal: Fasting glucose < 100 mg/dL; 2-hour post-load < 140 mg/dL.
  • Impaired glucose tolerance: fasting glucose 100-126 mg/dl; 2-hour post-load 140–199 mg/dL.
  • Diabetes mellitus: Fasting ≥ 126 mg/dL or 2-hour post-load ≥ 200 mg/dL .

 

 

Interpretation:

The patient's OGTT pattern on the graph matches the diabetic curve (persistent elevation above 200 mg/dL even after 2 hours), clearly meeting criteria for overt diabetes mellitus.

 

Other Options:

  • Option A. Symptoms of Diabetes mellitus with inconclusive blood glucose values: This applies when symptoms are present but glucose levels don’t conclusively meet diagnostic thresholds (not the case here, where the glucose is clearly high).
  • Option C. Diabetic nephropathy: This is a complication of diabetes involving kidney damage and is not diagnosed by OGTT . OGTT assesses glucose metabolism, not kidney function.
  • Option D. Follow-up of a case of Diabetes mellitus: OGTT is not recommended for follow-up of known diabetes cases. HbA1c, fasting glucose, and self-monitoring of blood glucose are the preferred methods for monitoring glycemic control in diagnosed patients.

 

Educational Objectives:

 

Difference between normal, impaired, and diabetic glucose values.

 

 

Ref: Harper 30/e:  p 195-196, 205.
